League+ steals leader (2025) * [[The league]] winner (2026) }} '''Jordy Tshimanga''' (born November 4, 1996) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Khasin Khuleguud]] of [[The League (Mongolia)|The League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]] and the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Tshimanga was born in [[Montreal]], the son of two Congolese parents. He has six brothers and sisters. Growing up, Tshimanga focused on football and began playing basketball in his teens. He attended [[MacDuffie School]] in [[Granby, Massachusetts]] and blossomed as a basketball player.{{cite news |last1=Archdeacon |first1=Tom |title=Archdeacon: Dayton Flyers newest big man has a personality that dwarfs his size 18 shoes, 7-foot-2 wingspan |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-dayton-flyers-newest-big-man-has-personality-that-dwarfs-his-size-shoes-foot-wingspan/4SiuAqpIO7IoFrYqbBgVQO/ |accessdate=March 25, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=August 24, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Tshimanga was a four-star selection by Scout.com and was rated as the No. 150 prospect in the senior class by Rivals.com. He was rated the No. 19 center in the country by Scout, No. 22 by 247Sports and No. 25 by ESPN.com. Tshimanga was ranked as the No. 15 prospect in New England by the New England Recruiting Report while ESPN.com rated him as the third-best prospect in the state of Massachusetts in 2016. He received offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Central Florida Knights men's basketball|Central Florida]], [[Louisiana State Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[Southern Methodist Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]], [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]], and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]].{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jordy-Tshimanga-69227/high-school-122100 |title=Jordy Tshimanga Recruiting Profile |date=July 11, 2016 |accessdate=November 14, 2017}} Following official visits to Minnesota, Nebraska and UNLV, Tshimanga committed to Cornhuskers on May 15, 2016.{{cite web |url=https://nebraska.rivals.com/news/2016-center-tshimanga-commits-to-nebraska |title=2016 center Tshimanga commits to Nebraska |date=May 16, 2016 |accessdate=November 14, 2017}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2016}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Jordy Tshimanga | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Montreal]], Quebec, Canada | highschool = MacDuffie School | feet = 6 | inches = 11 | weight = 270 | 40 = | commitdate = 05/16/2016 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 3 | 247 stars = 3 | 247 grade = 89 | espn grade = 79 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2016 | rivals ref title = 2016 Nebraska Basketball Commitment List | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN - Nebraska Cornhuskers Basketball Recruiting 2016 | rivals school = nebraska | scout s = 204 | espn schoolid = 158 | scout overall = xx, 19 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | rivals overall = 150, 17 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | 247sports overall = 150, 22 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | espn overall = xx, 25 ([[Power forward (basketball)|PF]]) | accessdate = 2016-12-01 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== Tshimanga appeared in all 31 games, averaging 5.0 points and 4.0 rebounds per game as a true freshman. He made significant strides throughout the season and played his best basketball during conference play, averaging 5.7 points and 4.2 rebounds per game, despite playing more than 20 minutes once in Big Ten play. Tshimanga led the Huskers in field goals percentage (.481) in conference play and was fourth on the team in rebounding.{{cite web |url=https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2016-17/player/jordy-tshimanga|title=Jordy Tshimanga Profile |date=March 17, 2017 |access-date=November 24, 2017}} He scored a career-high 15 points and grabbed 9 rebounds in just 24 minutes in Nebraska's 72–61 loss against Michigan State on February 2, 2017.{{cite web |url=http://www.omaha.com/huskers/mens-basketball/husker-notes-jordy-tshimanga-continues-to-show-progress-inside-spartan/article_b98156f7-2c47-5cf6-bc59-9a9f8bf0a734.html |title=Jordy Tshimanga continues to show progress inside; Spartan coach praises NU |first=Lee |last=Barfknecht |date=February 2, 2017 |work=Corn Nation |accessdate=November 24, 2017}} ===Sophomore year=== Tshimanga averaged 4.0 points and 4.6 rebounds per game his sophomore season. During the [[2017–18 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|2017–18 season]], Tshimanga temporarily left the team due to undisclosed "personal issues", missing two games in January 2018 before returning. Following the season, in July 2018, Tshimanga announced his intention to transfer from Nebraska.{{cite web| url = https://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/tshimanga-leaving-husker-basketball-program/article_d7cb7c9d-0f71-529c-84d8-a7452c7f4423.html| title = Tshimanga leaving Husker basketball program {{!}} Men's Basketball {{!}} journalstar.com}} ===Junior year=== Tshimanga ended up transferring to [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] and sat out the 2018–19 season as a redshirt. He missed the preseason with a knee injury and did not practice with the team until shortly before the Maui Invitational.{{cite web |last1=DiSano |first1=Chris |title=CHALK TALK: Dayton Transfers, Dambrot's Communication and the Emergence of Eyisi |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2020/1/17/mens-basketball-chalktalk-dayton-transfers-dambrots-communication-and-the-emrgence-of-eyisi.aspx |website=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] |accessdate=March 25, 2020 |date=January 17, 2020}} As a junior, Tshimanga averaged 3.0 points and 2.4 rebounds per game as a reserve.{{cite web |title=DAYTON MEN'S BASKETBALL 2020 NCAA TOURNAMENT CAPSULE |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/18439 |website=College Sports Madness |accessdate=March 25, 2020}} ===Senior year=== On February 9, 2021, Tshimanga posted 14 points and 12 rebounds in a 76–67 loss to [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]].{{cite news |title=VCU defeats Dayton 76-67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401286483 |access-date=June 18, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 9, 2021}} As a senior, he became a starter and averaged 6.7 points and 7.7 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Jablonski |first1=David |title=Dayton senior thanks UD, says he's ready for next journey |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-senior-thanks-ud-says-hes-ready-for-next-journey/KN4HFG6SXNFLJG5LIHUXOWRSI4/ |access-date=June 18, 2021 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=March 25, 2021}} Tshimanga was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] Academic Team.{{cite news |last1=Purves |first1=Michael |title=4 Dayton Flyers honored with postseason A-10 Conference awards |url=https://www.whio.com/sports/university-of-dayton-flyers/4-dayton-flyers-honored-with-postseason-a-10-conference-awards/DFULEDDX4ZA5FPR25FLZBLVUUY/ |access-date=June 18, 2021 |work=WHIO |date=March 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Charge / Iowa Wolves (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Tshimanga signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]] on October 23, 2021.{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}} He played four games and averaged 3.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 12.5 minutes.{{cite web|title=Saskatchewan Adds NBA G League Big Man, Jordy Tshimanga|url=https://www.cebl.ca/saskatchewan-adds-nba-g-league-big-man-jordy-tshimanga|website=CEBL.com|date=April 22, 2022|access-date=April 23, 2022}} On November 15, 2021, Tshimanga was traded from the Charge to the [[Iowa Wolves]],{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 15, 2021}} where he played 38 games and averaged 6.7 points and 6.5 rebounds in 17.3 minutes. During the season, he grabbed a career-high 17 rebounds on January 16 and a career-high 4 blocks on March 23, which the Wolves secure a top 5 rebounding total league-wide, with a team-high 186 total rebounds. ===Saskatchewan Rattlers (2022)=== On April 22, 2022, Tshimanga signed with the [[Saskatchewan Rattlers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]]. ===Return to Iowa (2023)=== On January 13, 2023, Tshimanga was reacquired by the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 13, 2023|access-date=January 13, 2023}} ===Cocodrilos de Caracas (2023)=== On April 3, 2023, Tshimanga signed with [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto|Venezuelan League]].{{cite web|title=JORDY TSHIMANGA REFUERZA LA PINTURA DE COCODRILOS DE CARACAS|url=https://canchalatina.com/2023/04/04/%F0%9F%87%BB%F0%9F%87%AA-jordy-tshimanga-reforzara-la-pintura-sauria/|website=CanchaLatina.com|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=April 4, 2023|language=Spanish}} ===Calgary Surge (2023)=== On July 5, 2023, Tshimanga signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=THE CALGARY SURGE ADD TWO MORE PLAYERS TO THEIR 2023 INAUGURAL ROSTER.|url=https://www.calgarysurge.ca/the-calgary-surge-have-signed-jordy-tshimanga-610-centre-from-montreal-quebec-and-64-guard-terry-henderson-jr-from-raleigh-north-carolina|website=CalgarySurge.ca|date=July 5, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} The team reached the CEBL Finals, losing to the [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]].{{cite web|title= Scarborough forward Isiaha Mike named game MVP after tallying 22 points, 9 boards|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/cebl/cebl-final-shooting-stars-surge-2023-recap-aug-13-1.6935048}} In August 2023, Tshimanga was selected as a Western Conference All-Star for the 2023 CEBL Clash in [[Québec City]]. The West won in a 107–102 victory.{{cite web|title=Western Conference Edges East 107-102 in Inaugural CEBL Clash|url=https://www.cebl.ca/western-conference-edges-east-107-102-in-inaugural-cebl-clash}} ===Trepça (2023–2024)=== On August 18, 2023, Tshimanga signed with [[KB Trepça|Trepça]] of the [[Kosovo Basketball Superleague]] and [[FIBA Europe Cup]].{{cite news|title=Trepça is strengthened with the Canadian Tshimanga|url=https://www.koha.net/en/sport/388971/trepca-forcohet-me-kanadezin-tshimanga/|website=Koha.net|date=August 18, 2023|access-date=August 18, 2023}} Tshimanga won the [[Kosovo Cup (basketball)|Kosovo Cup]] in the final against [[KB Prishtina|Prishtina]] where he was one of the key players with 15 rebounds and 11 points.{{cite news|title=Trepça fiton Kupën e Kosovës, hera e tretë me radhë|url=https://topsporti.com/artikulli/trepca-fiton-kupen-e-kosoves-hera-e-trete-me-radhe/kupa-e-kosoves|website=topsporti.com|date=February 17, 2024|language=sq|access-date=June 2, 2024}} He parted ways with Trepça in March 2024 because of doping accusations.{{cite news|title=Humbje e madhe për Trepçën, largohet përfundimisht Jordy Tshimanga|url=https://gazetablic.com/humbje-e-madhe-per-trepcen-largohet-perfundimisht-jordy-tshimanga/|website=gazetablic.com|date=March 8, 2024|access-date=June 2, 2024}} He was the best rebounder in the [[2023–24 Kosovo Basketball Superleague|2023-24 season]] averaging 10.0 rebounds per game. ===Return to Calgary (2024)=== On June 8, 2024, Tshimanga signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] for a second stint.{{cite web|title=The Calgary Surge Signs Three Additional Players to Their 2024 Roster|url=https://www.cebl.ca/the-calgary-surge-signs-three-additional-players-to-their-2024-roster|website=CEBL.ca|date=June 8, 2024|access-date=August 11, 2024}} ===Kaohsiung Steelers (2024–2025)=== On September 19, 2024, Tshimanga signed with the [[Kaohsiung 17LIVE Steelers]] of the [[P. League+]].{{cite web |title=鋼鐵人補進加拿大長人喬迪 將和老隊友艾賽亞重新攜手 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/4804407 |publisher=自由時報 |access-date=19 September 2024 |date=19 September 2024}} ===Taipei Taishin Mars (2025)=== On September 3, 2025, Tshimanga signed with the [[Taipei Taishin Mars]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).{{cite news |title=戰神延攬211公分防守悍將 齊曼加重返台灣鎮守禁區 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3027069 |accessdate=September 3, 2025 |work=ETtoday |date=September 3, 2025 }} On January 16, 2026, the [[Taipei Taishin Mars]] terminated the contract relationship with Tshimanga.{{cite news |title=掰了齊曼加！臺北台新戰神簽下昔日「全美五星高中生」救戰績 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3102204 |accessdate=January 16, 2026 |work=ETtoday |date=January 16, 2026 }} ==Career Jordy is the son of Florent Tshimanga and was born on November 4, 1996. He has two older brothers, Link Kabadyundi and Yannick Wak, and two sisters, Yasmine Bidikuindila and Florence Tshimanga. Tshimanga's family originates from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and he speaks three languages (English, French and [[Lingala]]). Tshimanga majored in psychology at Nebraska.{{cite web |url=http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211113403 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115015556/http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211113403 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 15, 2017 |title=Jordy Tshimanga Player Profile |date=August 17, 2017 |accessdate=November 14, 2017}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://daytonflyers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordy-tshimanga/10162 Dayton Flyers bio] *[https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2017-18/player/jordy-tshimanga Nebraska Cornhuskers bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tshimanga, Jordy}} [[Category:1996 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Montreal]] [[Category:Calgary Surge players]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in Kosovo]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in Venezuela]] [[Category:Canadian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Cleveland Charge players]] [[Category:Dayton Flyers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Iowa Wolves players]] [[Category:KB Trepça players]] [[Category:Kosovo Basketball Superleague players]] [[Category:Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Saskatchewan Rattlers players]] [[Category:21st-century Canadian sportsmen]] [[Category:Kaohsiung Steelers players]] [[Category:P.
